title: PowerPoint on Mac: reference SharePoint and OneDrive files when creating a presentation with Copilot Agent Mode
summary: Hold: licence assignment is not the only control over access to Copilot in PowerPoint. Microsoft's cited privacy documentation says connected-experience controls can also disable it on Mac. The roadmap details and the four published control paths and commands are supported.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans referencing SharePoint library and OneDrive folder files when creating a presentation with Agent Mode in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: You can now reference files saved in SharePoint libraries and OneDrive folders when creating a presentation with Agent Mode in PowerPoint.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot in PowerPoint recognises SharePoint and OneDrive files mentioned by file or document name and can use them as presentation context.
claims.quote: Copilot in PowerPoint can now recognize references to files stored in SharePoint and OneDrive when you mention them in your prompt, such as by file or document name.

claims.claim: Implicit file references were not previously supported for files in those locations.
claims.quote: Previously, these implicit file references were not supported for files stored in these locations.

claims.claim: The example tells users to reference a file by document name and/or owner.
claims.quote: In your prompt, reference a file saved in SharePoint or OneDrive by the document name and/or owner of the document.

claims.claim: Users need not first locate and manually attach the referenced file.
claims.quote: You can bring existing SharePoint and OneDrive content into your presentation workflow more naturally, without first locating the file and manually attaching it.

claims.claim: The sources do not state this feature's default state on arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: 'PowerPoint implicit file references SharePoint OneDrive default enabled admin switch Microsoft Graph PowerShell'. Read roadmap, release-note entry and Copilot overview. General gradual rollout is documented, but no feature-specific default is stated.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot surfaces only data the individual can access, respecting existing permissions rather than granting new access.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot presents only data that each individual can access using the same underlying controls for data access used in other Microsoft 365 services.

claims.claim: No mandatory admin action for this change is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot PowerPoint reference files by name SharePoint OneDrive license Basic admin setting disable implicit file references meter'. Read roadmap and full release-note entry; neither requires an administrator to act.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level control limiting selected SharePoint content in organisation-wide search and Copilot discovery.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery helps you limit discovery of content from specific SharePoint sites, including recently interacted files, in organization-wide search results and Microsoft Copilot responses while those reviews are taking place.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is not supported for OneDrive sites.
claims.quote: You can only apply this feature to SharePoint sites. It's not supported for OneDrive sites.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery changes discoverability, not existing permissions.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't change existing permissions. Users who already have access to content can continue to access that content directly.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The documentation does not specifically resolve whether Restricted Content Discovery stops files explicitly named in PowerPoint prompts.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Restricted Content Discovery PowerPoint prompt reference file by name'. Read RCD page and release-note entry. RCD covers tenant-wide discovery but excludes content already in use; neither identifies which case a named PowerPoint file falls into.

claims.claim: The release-note entry describes no new permission, identity or connection.
claims.quote: Searched: 'PowerPoint implicit file references SharePoint OneDrive default enabled admin switch Microsoft Graph PowerShell'. Read full release-note entry: it describes naming a cloud file as presentation context, not a new permission, identity or connection.

claims.claim: The release-note entry does not identify the component fetching the named file.
claims.quote: Searched: 'PowerPoint implicit file references SharePoint OneDrive default enabled admin switch Microsoft Graph PowerShell'. Read full release-note entry: it gives user prompts and file context, without specifying the fetching component.

claims.claim: The release note describes no background or scheduled operation or write to the source file.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot PowerPoint reference files by name SharePoint OneDrive license Basic admin setting disable implicit file references meter'. Read full feature entry: user requests creation using source information; no background, scheduled or source-write action.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery updates for sites with more than 500,000 items can take more than a week to fully process.
claims.quote: For sites with more than 500,000 items, an update to Restricted Content Discovery could take more than a week to fully process and reflect in search and Copilot experiences.

claims.claim: The surrounding Copilot in PowerPoint licensing has both add-on and Basic routes, reported as mixed with feature-specific entitlement left open.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) refers to users without the Copilot add-on license, but who have access to Copilot capabilities inside apps; Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) is the full add-on licensed experience.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on provides the full experience in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OneNote.
claims.quote: You have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; controls[1].note; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) users can use Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OneNote without the add-on.
claims.quote: You don't have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license but can use Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: Some features in both Basic and add-on experiences are subject to fair use limits.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic): Some features are subject to fair use limits. Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium): Some features are subject to fair use limits.

claims.claim: The feature's release-note entry and roadmap record name no licence tier or meter.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft 365 Copilot PowerPoint reference SharePoint files create presentation licensing requirements Copilot Credits pricing'. Read roadmap and full release-note entry; neither lists a licence tier or meter for the feature.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No feature-specific entitlement statement resolves whether Basic users can reference organisational files by name.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing PowerPoint Agent Mode reference files Basic Premium'. Read release entry, overview and licence-option excerpts. Overview distinguishes Graph grounding; no passage explicitly assigns this implicit-reference feature to Basic.

claims.claim: No meter or credit rate specifically for this file-reference feature is published in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft 365 Copilot Credits billing PowerPoint create presentations included'. Read release notes, Copilot overview and usage-based billing overview. Billing lists eligible services, including usage-based models in Office, but no rate for implicit file references.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery can be configured when the organisation is licensed for Copilot and has SharePoint Advanced Management available.
claims.quote: You can configure Restricted Content Discovery if your organization is licensed for Copilot and has SharePoint Advanced Management available.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is at SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites. Select the site you want to configure. Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: Enable Restricted Content Discovery for a site; Use PowerShell: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.claim: By default only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.claim: User licence assignment is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Users > Active users page. Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to. In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign.

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns a licence using Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
claims.quote: To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell. Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: A License Administrator or User Administrator is the minimum role stated for assigning licences.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: The add-on assignment controls that tier, not all Copilot in PowerPoint access, because Basic access does not require the add-on.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) license: You don't have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license but can use Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: Only Microsoft 365 admin center licence assignment changes who can use Copilot in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: If you turn off connected experiences that analyze your content ... Microsoft Copilot features won't be available ... PowerPoint ... This applies ... Windows, Mac, iOS, or Android devices.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with: 'The licence-assignment row governs the add-on tier, not all Copilot in PowerPoint access; Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) users can also use Copilot in PowerPoint without the add-on.' Remove 'Only'; the cited privacy page also documents connected-experience controls affecting PowerPoint on Mac.

claims.claim: The checklist's SharePoint and OneDrive permissions-review instructions have corresponding controls-table rows.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Review which SharePoint sites hold overshared content'; 'rely on fixing permissions there'. Table rows: Restricted Content Discovery and Copilot add-on licence assignment; neither changes permissions.
claims.fix: The Before rollout instructions to review overshared SharePoint content and fix OneDrive permissions name permissions controls with no corresponding table row. Restricted Content Discovery is not that row because it does not change permissions.
